newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch govt gives go-ahead to airport privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Dutch govt gives go-ahead to airport privatisation.

text.p: The Dutch government said on Friday it had approved in principle the partial privatisation of Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport.

But Home Affairs Minister Hans Dijkstal said a firm decision on the sale of part of the government's 75 percent stake would be delayed pending the outcome of the current debate on the future of the country's air infrastructure.

The public debate on airport expansion is due to be rounded off next month, but a government standpoint is not expected before next year at the earliest and could well be delayed until after general elections next May.
Dijkstal declined to comment on how much of its stake the government was likely to divest.
Schiphol president Hans Smits said at the presentation of the airport's annual results in April that management favoured public ownership of less than 50 percent.
The airport's other shareholders are the Amsterdam (22.8 percent) and Rotterdam (2.2 percent) city authorities.
